newsitem.title: USA: Four charged with cheating Florida investors.
newsitem.headline: Four charged with cheating Florida investors.

text.p: Federal prosecutors on Thursday charged four brokers and financial advisors, including ones formerly employed by American Express Co and Smith Barney Inc, with cheating elderly investors.

U.S. Attorney Charles Wilson said in a news release that Richard Frazier, 34, a former financial planner with American Express, had solicited small investors with promises of better returns on their holdings and had between late 1993 and July 1995 used their monies for his purposes.
The charges against Frazier include fraud and illegal money transactions and could result in prison terms and multiple fines of $250,000 each, Wilson said.

William Russel, 49, was accused of cheating his Smith Barney clients out of $160,000 with "Cayman Island off-shore gold deals" while working as stock broker in 1994 and 1995, Wilson said. Russel faces as much as 25 years imprisonment and fines as high as $1.25 million, if convicted, Wilson said.

Wilson also said that financial consultants John Dyer Jr, 52, and Robert DeMarco, 60, had struck plea bargains after being accused of defrauding more than 40 elderly investors out of more than $1 million by soliciting their investments with promises of high returns and using the investors money for their own purposes.

Both pled guilty to mail fraud, securities fraud, conspiracy and interstate transportation of stolen property and faces possible multiple sentences of imprisonment and fines of $250,000 for each count.
